summary: Acclaim's high-speed anti-gravity motorcycle racing series, spanning the Nintendo 64 original, a PC/N64 sequel, and two sixth-generation console follow-ups.

entries.title: Extreme-G

emulation.notes: Use Nintendo Classics for official access; N64 emulation is the offline preservation fallback.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Official Nintendo Classics emulation or N64 emulator upscaling

primary.platform: Nintendo Switch Online + Expansion Pack / Nintendo Classics
primary.why: The original Extreme-G was a Nintendo 64 release and was re-released through the Nintendo Classics service in 2024. The Nintendo Classics version is the current official route with modern access, while N64 emulation remains the fallback for offline preservation.
primary.how_to_play: Play through Nintendo Switch Online + Expansion Pack/Nintendo Classics, or use a Nintendo 64 emulator/original cartridge for offline preservation.

all_releases.reason: skip: authentic original route, but superseded for practical official play by Nintendo Classics.

all_releases.platform: Nintendo Switch Online + Expansion Pack / Nintendo Classics
all_releases.reason: primary: current official route and easiest modern play option.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: No sourced content difference between the N64 original and Nintendo Classics route.

entries.remaster_caveats: Nintendo Classics is a subscription/emulation route rather than a remaster.

entries.title: Extreme-G 2

emulation.notes: Use PC compatibility first; N64 emulation is a fallback.

primary.why: Extreme-G 2 was released on Nintendo 64 and Microsoft Windows. The Windows version has the highest output ceiling and no sourced content loss compared with Nintendo 64.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release on a compatibility setup; use Nintendo 64 emulation only if the PC version is unavailable.

all_releases.reason: skip: no sourced content advantage over PC and lower output ceiling.

all_releases.fidelity: PC release with higher output ceiling.
all_releases.reason: primary: highest-fidelity route for the sequel.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern remaster or official rerelease is sourced.

entries.title: XGIII: Extreme G Racing

emulation.notes: Use Dolphin for the primary route; PCSX2 is a fallback for the PS2 version.

primary.why: XGIII: Extreme G Racing was released for PlayStation 2 and GameCube. With no sourced content differences, GameCube via Dolphin is the preferred high-fidelity emulation route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the GameCube version on original hardware or Dolphin with internal resolution scaling; use PlayStation 2/PCSX2 as a fallback.

all_releases.reason: skip: no sourced content advantage over GameCube and less convenient than Dolphin for this pick.

all_releases.fidelity: Original GameCube release, strong Dolphin emulation route.
all_releases.reason: primary: preferred high-fidelity emulation route with complete content.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: No sourced content difference between PS2 and GameCube.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern remaster or official rerelease is sourced.

entries.title: XGRA: Extreme-G Racing Association

emulation.notes: Use original Xbox hardware or xemu for the primary route; Dolphin is a strong fallback if xemu compatibility is imperfect.

primary.why: XGRA was released on PlayStation 2, Xbox, and GameCube. No sourced platform-exclusive content is listed, so the Xbox version is the primary console route for strongest original hardware output, with emulation available through xemu as compatibility permits.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Xbox version on original hardware or xemu if compatible; use Dolphin or PCSX2 as platform fallbacks.

all_releases.reason: skip: no sourced content advantage over Xbox.
primary: strongest original console hardware route with complete content.
skip: strong preservation route, but no sourced content advantage over Xbox.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern remaster or official rerelease is sourced.
